summary: Established an AIDE-based integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 10). Installed aide, verified the distro-default aide.conf already covers /etc comprehensively (explicit rules for ~90 paths plus a catch-all "/etc PERMS"), initialized the database, and confirmed detection works by modifying /etc/hosts and observing AIDE flag it, then restoring and re-baselining cleanly (36014 entries, zero diffs). Added /etc/cron.daily/aide-check to run daily checks and log results via logger for ongoing reporting. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and aide.db.gz hash pre-restart, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until the node returned, proved the boot_id changed, and confirmed the AIDE database hash was unchanged and `aide --check` still reports no differences post-reboot, with crond active and the daily script intact.

evidence.requirement: Integrity baseline established for /etc on node1
evidence.summary: AIDE installed with distro-default config covering /etc extensively; database initialized (36014 entries) and activated; aide --check reports no differences against the fresh baseline.

evidence.requirement: Later changes to /etc files can be identified and reported
evidence.summary: Modifying /etc/hosts was correctly flagged by aide --check as a changed entry; after revert the file matched baseline again. A daily cron job (/etc/cron.daily/aide-check) was added to run aide --check and log results via logger for ongoing reporting; its own addition to /etc/cron.daily was itself correctly detected by AIDE, proving the reporting mechanism and detection both work.

evidence.requirement: Final baseline reflects the intended healthy /etc state
evidence.summary: Baseline re-initialized after adding the cron script, giving a clean aide --check (36014 entries, zero differences) as the authoritative healthy state going into the restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline captured pre-restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146 and aide.db.gz SHA256 81c87f5b... as the pre-restart healthy state.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: restart acknowledged and executed one node at a time
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup so acknowledgement returned before the connection dropped; exec stream closed as node1 went down, confirming the reboot took effect.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: boot identity proven changed
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeouts while node1 was down, then exec succeeded again with a new boot_id (1eaaabc1-6a58-45a1-bb5d-d53fb253035c), differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: post-restart recovery of required services/data verified
evidence.summary: Post-reboot, aide.db.gz SHA256 matched the pre-restart value exactly (data persisted), aide --check still reported NO differences against live /etc, crond was active, and the daily reporting script /etc/cron.daily/aide-check was intact — confirming full recovery of the integrity-baseline capability.
